transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Cleveland, Ohio, I'm Dale Willman.
President Trump is spending the final days of the midterms
imploring Republicans to vote in key races.
NPR's Stephen Fowler reports from a rally in Dubuque, Iowa.
At his penultimate in-person event,
Trump did what Trump normally does.
Speak at length about many topics,
from touting his accomplishments in office to attacking Democrats,
and defended high gas prices caused by the ongoing war in Iran.
To be honest, I thought it would go up much higher than it went up.
And, you know, I don't want to say, because they'll say,
"Oh, he thinks it's a very small price to pay for the security of this country."
Also in the nearly two-hour speech,
Trump commented on Republican U.S. Senate nominee Ashley Henson's weight,
heckled protesters as "stupid,"
and promised to send Americans money if Republicans kept control of Congress,
something he cannot do.
Stephen Fowler, NPR News, Dubuque, Iowa.
Michigan is a key battleground in Tuesday's midterms,
with critical House and Senate races that could decide control of Congress.
This weekend, House Speaker Mike Johnson was in Michigan
campaigning for Republicans, NPR's Sam Greenglass reports.
Macomb County is one of the most purple places in purple Michigan.
Democrats see an open House seat here as a top target to flip.
At a Builders and Contractors Association near a sprawling Chrysler plant,
Speaker Johnson framed the battle for Congress as existential.
What I'm telling you is, in the next Congress, it begins January 3rd.
We are no longer going to be arguing about marginal tax rates.
We're not going to be debating shades of difference in foreign policy and regulation.
We're going to be talking about whether we're going to maintain the republic,
the very foundations of America.
Also speaking was Republican former Congressman Mike Rogers.
He's in a closely watched race for U.S. Senate with Democrat Abdul El-Sayed.
Democrats need to net just three House seats nationally to reclaim the chamber.
Sam Greenglass, NPR News, Sterling Heights, Michigan.
In Houston, the federal agent who struck a Mexican construction worker with his vehicle last month
is expected to surrender himself Monday morning.
That's according to his attorney.
The agent is facing state charges of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon.
Houston Public Media's Bianca Seward has our reports.
ICE agent Mario Morales is accused of intentionally striking Miguel Parra Hernandez
with his car in early October.
Last week, a Harris County grand jury indicted Morales,
a rare instance of state charges being brought against a federal agent.
Morales' lawyer David Lyndon Muth calls the indictment political prosecution.
This was nothing more than an accident.
And the driving force behind this accident is somebody who fled from law enforcement.
The collision left Parra Hernandez with a broken leg and ankle.
Body camera footage released Friday shows Morales' car pursuing Parra Hernandez,
striking him from behind and coming to a stop several feet after running him over.
If Morales is convicted, he faces up to 20 years in prison.
For NPR News, I'm Bianca Seward in Houston.
And you're listening to NPR News.
There were a number of mass shootings in cities across the U.S. this Halloween weekend.
Police in Dallas say four people were killed and 15 others injured
following separate incidents in a nightlife district.
There were also other shootings in a number of college towns,
including Bloomington, Illinois, Birmingham, Alabama, and Fayetteville, Arkansas.
A Swedish runner secured a win in the men's race of the New York City Marathon today
and Pierre's Chantalice Duster reports on that annual race.
Andreas Almgren of Sweden won the men's race on Sunday with a time of two hours,
six minutes, and one second.
He beat Jamin Abraham Kripa of Italy by 13 seconds, who finished in second place.
This was both men's first New York City Marathon debut.
Sheila Shevkarui, a 2024 champion from Kenya, won the women's race at two hours,
24 minutes, and 36 seconds.
Nearly 60,000 runners from around the world are estimated to have participated
in the marathon that spans 26.2 miles.
The race spanned all five boroughs and across five bridges.
Champions of the women's and men's open division will receive $100,000 each.
Champions in the women's and men's wheelchair division will receive $50,000 each.
Chantalice Duster, NPR News.
Twenty-year-old Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli has become the youngest champion
in the history of Formula One racing.
He is also the first Italian to win that title since Alberto Ascari in 1953.
He took the lead following the Mexico City Grand Prix on Sunday.
The previous youngest champion was 23 years old.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.

topics.text: Trump's Dubuque, Iowa rally defends high gas prices and attacks Democrats before midterms
House Speaker Mike Johnson campaigns in Macomb County, Michigan for Republican candidates
Houston ICE agent Mario Morales expected to surrender after indictment for striking construction worker
Mass shootings in Dallas and several college towns leave multiple dead and injured over Halloween weekend
Swedish runner Andreas Almgren wins men's New York City Marathon; Sheila Shevkarui wins women's race
Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest Formula One champion after Mexico City Grand Prix
